data.one_liner: Flutter widget providing a searchable, sortable, and paginated list UI.
data.what_it_does: It renders a list view combined with a customizable search field, allowing users to filter items synchronously or asynchronously. It also supports expansion groups, slivers, pull-to-refresh, and pagination.
use_when: You need to display a list of items with an integrated search bar.
You require support for asynchronous data sources and filtering.
You need features like pagination, pull-to-refresh, or expansion groups out-of-the-box.
avoid_when: You need a standard non-searchable list view where custom search is unnecessary.
You are building your own highly custom search architecture with explicit controllers and custom animations.
strengths: Supports synchronous and asynchronous data loading and filtering.
Provides multiple constructors including slivers and expansion groups.
Highly customizable search field and state widgets.
weaknesses: Tied specifically to its own list implementation wrapper, which may limit deep customization of underlying scroll physics or layout.
data.minimal_example:
SearchableList<Actor>(
  initialList: actors,
  itemBuilder: (actor) => ActorItem(actor: actor),
  filter: (query) => actors
      .where((a) => a.name.toLowerCase().contains(query.toLowerCase()))
      .toList(),
  emptyWidget: const Center(child: Text('No results')),
  inputDecoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Search actor'),
)
